bio_html: Subhrajit (Jit) Choudhury is a Ph.D. student in Public Management and Policy at Georgia State University's Andrew Young School of Policy Studies, advised by William Resh. Before the doctoral study, he served in the West Bengal Civil Services, where he managed large-scale public distribution operations, and earned an MSc in Financial Economics from the Madras School of Economics. His research sits at the intersection of institutional theory and behavioral public administration and seeks to understand why people act as they do in government, how public organizations perform, and how rules and structures change both. He also works with large-scale federal workforce data, examining how institutional change and reform show up in hiring, separations, and the composition of the federal workforce. As a graduate research assistant at CLEAR, Jit helps build and maintain INSIGHT+, the center's relational database of federal personnel and hiring data, including its schema design, data pipelines, validation, and regular updates. He also supports the Accountability and Reform Research Consortium (ARRC) by managing its online presence and research communications.
